package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised at the source code level to include a sophisticated backdoor (SUNBURST), which was compiled, signed, and distributed as a legitimate update through the official SolarWinds patch management system. This allowed attackers to gain persistent, covert access to thousands of organizations' networks by enabling remote command execution, data exfiltration, and lateral movement.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At service startup, the code checks for security tools and sandbox environments, waits a random interval to evade detection, then initiates outbound HTTPS connections to attacker-controlled C2 domains, downloads additional payloads, and executes them, resulting in persistent covert remote access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs anti-analysis checks to detect security tools or sandbox environments, introduces randomized execution delays to evade automated detection, and establishes outbound network connections to attacker-controlled domains to download and execute further payloads. These behaviors are highly atypical for legitimate monitoring software and are indicative of advanced persistent threat activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal SolarWinds Orion code should not perform anti-analysis or sandbox checks, should not introduce random execution delays, and should never contact unknown or suspicious external domains for instructions or payloads. Legitimate updates should not enable remote code execution or download additional code from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate enterprise software may check for debuggers or sandboxes for licensing enforcement or anti-piracy, but such checks are not expected in monitoring software, and legitimate software does not use these checks in conjunction with covert network communications to unknown domains or dynamic code execution.
key_indicators: Anti-analysis and sandbox environment checks at service startup
Randomized execution delays before initiating network activity
Outbound HTTPS connections to attacker-controlled or algorithmically generated domains
Dynamic download and execution of remote payloads within a signed production binary
Obfuscated or hidden code paths not present in legitimate versions

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to SolarWinds source code repository and inserts backdoor logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor is compiled and signed as part of legitimate update.

attack_chain.action: Compromised update is distributed to customers via official patch management system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is deployed in thousands of customer environments.

attack_chain.action: On service startup, backdoor code checks for safe execution environment, delays, and contacts C2.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishes covert remote access for attacker.

attack_chain.action: Attacker issues commands or delivers additional payloads to compromised systems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise and lateral movement within victim networks.

behavioral_signatures: Anti-analysis or sandbox/AV checks at service startup in Orion binaries
Randomized execution delays before any network activity
Unexpected outbound HTTPS connections to newly registered or algorithmically generated domains
Dynamic code execution or payload download in a signed monitoring tool binary
Obfuscated or hidden code paths not present in previous legitimate versions
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in signed binaries, especially SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll
Presence of obfuscated or anti-analysis logic in production code
Unexplained new DLLs or code blocks in update packages
File hashes of known compromised versions (as published by SolarWinds advisories)
network_indicators: Connections to known SUNBURST C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud[.]com)
DNS queries to algorithmically generated or recently registered domains associated with SUNBURST
Unusual outbound HTTP/S traffic from Orion servers to external IPs not previously contacted
Use of HTTP/S User-Agent strings or request patterns matching SUNBURST activity
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected outbound network connections from Orion servers, especially to suspicious or recently registered domains such as avsvmcloud[.]com. Analyze update packages and binaries for anti-analysis logic, randomized execution delays, and code that downloads or executes remote payloads. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes in signed binaries, particularly SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll. Employ advanced static and behavioral analysis to identify hidden backdoors or anomalous code paths in software updates. Correlate network indicators with known SUNBURST C2 infrastructure and monitor for DNS queries to algorithmically generated domains.
